summary:
I have now traced the complete flow. Here is the full picture for POST /api/owners.

## Summary of execution order

Active config: `spring.profiles.active=h2,spring-data-jpa` and `petclinic.security.enable=false` (`src/main/resources/application.properties:20,49`). So the repository implementation used at runtime is the Spring Data JPA proxy of `SpringDataOwnerRepository`, and security is the permit-all chain (`DisableSecurityConfig`), meaning `@PreAuthorize` is not enforced (method security is only enabled inside the security-enabled config).

The endpoint path is `/api/owners`: the controller is `@RequestMapping("/api")` and the generated interface maps `POST /owners`.

---

## 1. The @RestController method handling POST /api/owners

`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`

The class (lines 53-56) is `@RestController @RequestMapping("/api")` implementing `OwnersApi`. The handler is `addOwner` (lines 103-116):

```java
@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")
@Override
public ResponseEntity<OwnerDto> addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto) {
    HttpHeaders headers = new HttpHeaders();
    Owner owner = ownerMapper.toOwner(ownerFieldsDto);
    owner.setCustomerCode(CustomerCode.of(owner, this.clinicService.findAllOwners()));
    this.clinicService.saveOwner(owner);
    AUDIT.info("owner created id={} customerCode={} registrationDate={}",
        owner.getId(), owner.getCustomerCode(), owner.getRegistrationDate());
    OwnerDto ownerDto = ownerMapper.toOwnerDto(owner);
    headers.setLocation(UriComponentsBuilder.newInstance()
        .path("/api/owners/{id}").buildAndExpand(owner.getId()).toUri());
    return new ResponseEntity<>(ownerDto, headers, HttpStatus.CREATED);
}
```

The actual HTTP mapping and `@Valid` live on the generated interface default method it overrides — `target/generated-sources/openapi/.../rest/api/OwnersApi.java:79-87`:

```java
@RequestMapping(method = RequestMethod.POST, value = OwnersApi.PATH_ADD_OWNER, // "/owners"
    produces = { "application/json" }, consumes = { "application/json" })
default ResponseEntity<OwnerDto> addOwner(
    @Parameter(...) @Valid @RequestBody OwnerFieldsDto ownerFieldsDto) { ... }
```

The interface is annotated `@Validated` (class level, line 44), which is what triggers request-body bean validation.

---

## 2. Request body DTO and its Bean Validation constraints

The bound body type is `OwnerFieldsDto` — `target/generated-sources/openapi/.../rest/dto/OwnerFieldsDto.java`. Constraints are declared on the getters:

- `firstName` (line 73): `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$") @Size(min = 1, max = 30)`
- `lastName` (line 94): `@NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$") @Size(min = 1, max = 30)`
- `address` (line 115): `@NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 255)`
- `city` (line 136): `@NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 80)`
- `telephone` (line 157): `@NotNull @Size(min = 1, max = 20)`
- `email` (line 178): `@Size(max = 255) @jakarta.validation.constraints.Email` (optional)
- `postcode` (line 199): `@Pattern(regexp = "^[0-9]{4}$")` (optional; 4 digits)
- `registrationDate` (line 220): `@Valid` only, optional `LocalDate`
- `sharesHousehold` (line 242): no constraints; optional `Boolean` — used only by an out-of-scope duplicate/household exemption feature

Note: the persistent entity `Owner` (`src/main/java/.../model/Owner.java`) carries its own constraints too, which apply on JPA persist/flush: `address` `@NotEmpty` (40), `city` `@NotEmpty` (44), `telephone` `@NotEmpty @Pattern(regexp="^\\+[0-9]{8,15}$", message="Phone number must be in E.164 format")` (48-49), plus `firstName`/`lastName` `@NotEmpty` from `Person` (`model/Person.java:32,36`). So the telephone must already be in E.164 form by the time it is saved — this is why the advice below rewrites it.

---

## 3. Service layer method(s)

`src/main/java/.../service/ClinicServiceImpl.java` — the controller calls two methods:

`findAllOwners()` (lines 126-129, used to compute the customer code and by several aspects):
```java
@Transactional(readOnly = true)
public Collection<Owner> findAllOwners() throws DataAccessException {
    return ownerRepository.findAll();
}
```

`saveOwner(owner)` (lines 232-237):
```java
@Transactional
public void saveOwner(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
    ownerRepository.save(owner);
}
```

---

## 4. Repository calls, lifecycle callbacks, events, other side-effects

Repository interface: `src/main/java/.../repository/OwnerRepository.java`. At runtime (profile `spring-data-jpa`) the implementation is the Spring Data proxy of `SpringDataOwnerRepository` (`.../repository/springdatajpa/SpringDataOwnerRepository.java`), whose `save` is the default `JpaRepository.save` (persist for new entities). The `@Profile("jpa")` alternative `JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl.save` (lines 92-100) does `em.persist` when id is null, else `em.merge`.

There are **no** entity lifecycle callbacks (`@PrePersist`/`@PreUpdate`/`@EntityListeners`) and **no** `ApplicationEventPublisher` usage anywhere in `src/main/java` (grep returned nothing).

Non-obvious side-effects that mutate the owner during creation:

- Mapper `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (`target/generated-sources/annotations/.../OwnerMapperImpl.java:78-95`) copies fields via setters, which triggers:
  - `Owner.setRegistrationDate` (`model/Owner.java:88-91`) — defaults null to `LocalDate.now()` and rolls weekends forward via `BusinessDay.onOrNextBusinessDay` (`util/BusinessDay.java:31-37`).
  - `Owner.setEmail` (`model/Owner.java:97-99`) — lower-cases the email.
- `CustomerCode.of(owner, findAllOwners())` (`rest/controller/v1/CustomerCode.java:17-22`) — builds `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` where NNNN is a per-city sequence (count of existing owners in that city + 1), then `owner.setCustomerCode(...)`.
- `AUDIT` logger (`OwnerRestControllerV1.java:58,110`) writes an audit line after save.

An additional aspect fires **inside** `saveOwner` — see #5 (`OwnerIdentityUniquenessAspect`).

---

## 5. Custom validators, @ControllerAdvice, aspects/interceptors

### Bean-binding Validators registered via @InitBinder (run during request-body binding, and they mutate the payload)

`src/main/java/.../rest/advice/OwnerFieldsValidationAdvice.java` — `@ControllerAdvice implements Validator`, supports `OwnerFieldsDto`. ## Net order of validations and side-effects for a successful POST /api/owners

1. Security filter chain — permit-all (or Basic auth + `ROLE_OWNER_ADMIN` if security enabled).
2. Body deserialized to `OwnerFieldsDto`; `@Valid`/`@Validated` runs JSR-380 constraints (section 2) plus the two `@InitBinder` Validators, which also normalize `address` and rewrite `telephone` to E.164. Any failure → `MethodArgumentNotValidException` → 400 via `ExceptionControllerAdvice`.
3. `@Before` controller aspects: daily limit (429 at ≥100) and city capacity (409 at ≥50).
4. Handler body: map DTO→`Owner` (registrationDate defaulting/business-day roll, email lower-casing), compute+set `customerCode`, then `clinicService.saveOwner`.
5. `@Before` service aspect: identity-uniqueness (409 on duplicate telephone|email key).
6. `ownerRepository.save` → JPA persist; entity-level `@NotEmpty`/E.164 `@Pattern` constraints enforced on flush.
7. AUDIT log line.
8. Map `Owner`→`OwnerDto` with four `@AfterMapping` derivations; then three `@AfterReturning` aspects enrich the DTO (membershipNumber, namesakeCount/membershipLevel, bulkSignupWarning).
9. Return `201 Created` with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

No entity lifecycle callbacks and no application events are involved anywhere in this flow.

## 2. Request-body binding & validation (on `OwnerFieldsDto`)
Triggered by `@Valid`/`@Validated`. All failures here become a **400** via `ExceptionControllerAdvice.handleMethodArgumentNotValidException`.

**a. JSR-380 bean constraints on the DTO:**
- `firstName` — `@NotNull`, `@Pattern` (letters, up to 3 words), `@Size(1..30)`
- `lastName` — `@NotNull`, `@Pattern` (letters, optional trailing `.`), `@Size(1..30)`
- `address` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..255)`
- `city` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..80)`
- `telephone` — `@NotNull`, `@Size(1..20)`
- `email` — `@Size(max 255)`, `@Email` (optional)
- `postcode` — `@Pattern("^[0-9]{4}$")` (optional)

**b. `@InitBinder` custom `Validator`s (these also MUTATE the payload):**
- `OwnerFieldsValidationAdvice` — rejects blank required fields; **normalizes `address`** (uppercase, collapse whitespace, expand ST/RD/AVE via `AddressNormalizer`); **rewrites `telephone` to E.164** via `E164Telephone.toE164` (assumes +61, drops leading 0, validates 8–15 digits), rejecting telephone if no valid E.164 can be formed.

## 3. `@Before` aspects on the controller method (pre-checks, before handler body)
- `OwnerDailyLimitAdvice` — counts owners registered today; throws **429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS** at ≥100.
- `OwnerCityCapacityAdvice` — counts owners in the same (normalized) city; throws **409 CONFLICT** at ≥50.

## 4. Handler body (`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`)
- **Map DTO → `Owner`** via `OwnerMapper.toOwner`, whose setters cause side-effects:
  - `setRegistrationDate` — defaults null to `LocalDate.now()` and rolls weekends forward to the next business day (`BusinessDay`).
  - `setEmail` — lower-cases the email.
- **Compute and set `customerCode`** = `CustomerCode.of(owner, findAllOwners())` → `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, where `NNNN` is a per-city sequence (requires reading all existing owners).
- Call `clinicService.saveOwner(owner)`.

## 5. `@Before` aspect on the service method
- `OwnerIdentityUniquenessAspect` (on `saveOwner`) — for new owners, builds key `telephone|email|` and throws **409 CONFLICT** if any existing owner matches.

## 6. Persistence
- `ownerRepository.save(owner)` → JPA persist. On flush, **entity-level constraints on `Owner`/`Person`** are enforced: `firstName`/`lastName`/`address`/`city` `@NotEmpty`, and `telephone` `@NotEmpty` + `@Pattern` requiring E.164 format (`^\+[0-9]{8,15}$`) — which passes only because step 2b rewrote it.

## 7. Audit side-effect
- `AUDIT` logger writes an audit line (`owner created id=… customerCode=… registrationDate=…`).

## 8. Response DTO enrichment (no storage effect)
- **Map `Owner` → `OwnerDto`** via `OwnerMapper.toOwnerDto`, with four `@AfterMapping` derivations: `householdId`, `identityKey`, `locality`, `contactPreference`.
- Three `@AfterReturning` aspects enrich the returned DTO: `OwnerMembershipNumberAdvice` (`membershipNumber`), `OwnerNamesakeCountAdvice` (`namesakeCount`, `membershipLevel`), `OwnerBulkSignupWarningAdvice` (`bulkSignupWarning` when >80 created today).

## 9. Response
- Return **201 Created** with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

**Notably absent:** there are no JPA lifecycle callbacks (`@PrePersist`/`@PreUpdate`/`@EntityListeners`) and no application events anywhere in this flow.
